LRT opened two separate submission forms on 2 October 2013: one for artists and another for songwriters to submit their entries [d40165141s4p0].
The submission deadline for both artist and songwriter applications concluded on 15 November 2013 [d40165141s4p0].
A total of 106 song submissions were received and 16 potential Eurovision songs were selected and announced for listening and voting on 12 January 2014 [d40165141s4p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Detail how voting power was distributed in each stage of the competition that year: specify the percentage or point allocation between domestic jury panels, any international juries, and public televote/SMS/app voting in heats, semi-finals and the final, and note whether juries or televote had veto or supermajority privileges.
sub_answers.text:
The results of each of the 12 shows were determined by a 50/50 combination of votes from a jury panel and public televoting [d40165141s3p0].
The jury votes in all shows consisted of a combination of a Lithuanian jury panel and an international jury panel [d40165141s3p0].
From the second show to the semi-final the Lithuanian panel came to a consensus to assign one set of points which were added to the international panel results, while the international panel members assigned points in descending order for their rankings [d40165141s3p0].
The public could vote through telephone and SMS, and the ranking developed by both jury and public voting was converted to points from 1-8, 10 and 12 and assigned based on the number of competing artists in the respective show [d40165141s3p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe the stated mechanisms for breaking ties and for determining which acts progressed between rounds that year: include explicit tie-break rules (e.g., higher jury score, higher televote, head-to-head comparisons), quota or wildcard provisions, minimum score thresholds, and any rule for replacing withdrawn/disqualified qualifiers.
sub_answers.text:
Ties in the elimination shows and the semi-final were decided in favour of the entry that received the most votes from the public [d40165141s3p0].
In the final, a tie was decided in favour of the entry that was awarded the most points by the jury [d40165141s3p0].
From the second and third shows, five of ten artists were eliminated in each show, and during each of the fourth to tenth shows one artist was eliminated with the remaining three artists advancing in the competition [d40165141s3p0].
Starting from the fifth show, 16 potential Eurovision songs competed weekly and a total of 13 songs were eliminated following the tenth show, leaving three songs remaining, with the semi-final selecting only the winning song from those three and the final selecting the winning artist-song combination from the remaining three artists [d40165141s3p0].
